name: Quartz
description: Quartz is one of the most abundant minerals in Earth's crust. It is known for its hexagonal crystal structure and wide variety of colors.
marketValue: $10 - $500 depending on specimen size and quality
funFacts: Quartz crystals are used in watches because they vibrate at precise frequencies when an electric current is applied.
history: Ancient Greeks believed quartz was ice that had frozen so hard it would never melt.

name: Amethyst
composition: SiO₂ with trace amounts of iron
description: Amethyst is the purple variety of quartz and is highly prized for its deep violet hue.
uses: Gemstone jewelry, ornamental pieces, spiritual practices.
funFacts: The name comes from the Ancient Greek word 'amethystos', meaning 'not intoxicated'.
history: In ancient times, it was believed that wearing amethyst could prevent drunkenness.

name: Ruby
description: Rubies are among the most valuable gemstones in the world, known for their intense red color and exceptional hardness.
uses: High-end jewelry, precision lasers, industrial bearings.
funFacts: The 'Sunrise Ruby' is the world's most expensive ruby, selling for over $30 million.
history: In ancient Sanskrit, rubies were called 'ratnaraj', meaning 'king of precious stones'.

name: Sapphire
description: Sapphire is a precious gemstone, a variety of the mineral corundum, consisting of aluminum oxide with trace amounts of elements such as iron, titanium, chromium, vanadium, or magnesium.
funFacts: The most famous sapphire is the 12-carat blue sapphire in Princess Diana's engagement ring.
history: For centuries, sapphires have symbolized royalty, romance, and divine favor.

name: Obsidian
description: Obsidian is a naturally occurring volcanic glass formed when felsic lava extruded from a volcano cools rapidly with minimal crystal growth.
funFacts: Obsidian can be fractured to produce a cutting edge thinner and sharper than a surgical steel scalpel.
history: Pre-Columbian Mesoamericans used obsidian for weapons, tools, and decorative objects.

name: Granite
description: Granite is a coarse-grained igneous rock composed mostly of quartz, alkali feldspar, and plagioclase.
funFacts: The base of the Statue of Liberty is made of granite from Stony Creek, Connecticut.
history: Ancient Egyptians used granite to build some of their most iconic structures, including the pyramids.

name: Emerald
description: Emerald is a gemstone and a variety of the mineral beryl colored green by trace amounts of chromium and sometimes vanadium.
funFacts: Most emeralds have tiny fractures called 'jardin' (French for garden) that prove they are natural.
history: Cleopatra was known for her love of emeralds and claimed all emerald mines in Egypt as her own.

name: Topaz
description: Topaz is a silicate mineral of aluminum and fluorine. It is one of the hardest naturally occurring minerals.
marketValue: $10 - $1,000 per carat (Imperial Topaz is most valuable)
funFacts: Pure topaz is colorless; the colors are caused by impurities or defects in the crystal structure.
history: Ancient Greeks believed that topaz could increase strength and make the wearer invisible.

name: Opal
description: Opal is a hydrated amorphous form of silica. Its internal structure makes it diffract light, resulting in a play of colors.
funFacts: Opal is the only gemstone that can contain up to 21% water within its structure.
history: Arabic legends say that opals fall from the sky in flashes of lightning.

name: Jade
description: Jade is an ornamental mineral, mostly known for its green varieties. It refers to two different silicate minerals: nephrite and jadeite.
marketValue: $5 - $3,000+ per carat (Imperial Jade is most expensive)
funFacts: Jade is exceptionally tough and was used for axe heads and weapons in prehistoric times.
history: In Chinese culture, jade is considered the 'Imperial Gem' and is associated with immortality and luck.
